Isolated figures do exist, five quarters in all, never contiguous for more than two quarters: (1) Bausch Health 3Q20 earnings presentation prose, 'VYZULTA reported $13M in revenue or reported revenue growth of 30% vs. 3Q19' (2020Q3, scope not stated); (2) Bausch + Lomb 2Q23 earnings presentation, constant-currency reconciliation appendix, row 'Vyzulta 15 - 15 12 3 25% 3 25%' ($M: 2Q23 reported 15, 2Q22 reported 12); (3) Bausch + Lomb 3Q23 earnings presentation, same appendix, row 'Vyzulta 19 1 20 13 6 46% 7 54%' ($M: 3Q23 reported 19, 3Q22 reported 13). That gives 2020Q3 13, 2022Q2 12, 2022Q3 13, 2023Q2 15, 2023Q3 19 (company-wide revenue, FX-adjusted, so worldwide). The 1Q23 and 4Q23 decks give only growth rates ('Vyzulta saw +25% reported revenue growth'), and no deck from 1Q24 to 2Q26 has a Vyzulta row. Two two-quarter fragments years after launch are not a launch-uptake series, so the product stays excluded; the figures are recorded here for anyone who wants a scale check. The royalty holder Nicox SA reported only royalty revenue (tiered 6-12%, combined with ZERVIATE in its 'net revenue') and stopped quarterly reporting after selling the royalty to Soleus Capital in 2024.

source_quote: Bayer Annual Report 2025, note B 4/6 'Sales by product - Pharmaceuticals' (EUR million, 2024 2025): ... Gadovist product family 428 415; Stivarga 463 338; Glucobay 166 177; Other 2,768 2,644 (no Vitrakvi line). Business description: 'Oncology ... Nexavar, Nubeqa, Stivarga, Vitrakvi, Xofigo'.
details: Bayer, the sole worldwide marketer since it took exclusive global rights after Lilly acquired Loxo Oncology (Lilly Q1 2019 release: 'Lilly is eligible to receive milestones and royalties from Bayer on future sales of Vitrakvi'), prints no Vitrakvi sales figure. Its most detailed product list is the note 'Sales by product - Pharmaceuticals' in the Annual Report (Eylea, Nubeqa, Xarelto, Kerendia, Gadovist product family, Stivarga, Glucobay and others, then 'Other' 2,768/2,644 for 2024/2025); Vitrakvi is not named and sits in 'Other'. In the AR 2025 text Vitrakvi appears only in the business description (Oncology: 'Nexavar, Nubeqa, Stivarga, Vitrakvi, Xofigo') and the patent table. No isolated figure exists in any issuer document found: no quarter, half-year or full-year Vitrakvi amount, not even in prose. Bayer management declined to disclose patient numbers on the Q2 2019 call (transcript, not citable). Loxo Oncology (co-promoter until 2019-02) filed no periodic report after approval; Lilly records only milestone/royalty income from Bayer and never prints Vitrakvi sales.

source_quote: Sol-Gel Technologies Form 20-F for 2025, Operating Results, Revenues: During the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, we recognized revenues from royalties related to our collaboration agreements with Galderma in the amounts of $1.2 million, $1.6 million, and $0.7 million, respectively, and revenues from sale of IP and license, mainly from agreements with Padagis, Beimei and Searchlight in the amounts of $0.4 million, $9.8 million, and $18.6 million, respectively.
details: Epsolay (approved 2022-04-22) was sold in the U.S. by Galderma under a licence from Sol-Gel until the licence was mutually terminated and the U.S. rights were sold to Mayne Pharma (announced 2025-04-17; Mayne relaunched it in its FY2026, July 2025 to June 2026). None of the three companies prints an Epsolay sales figure. Sol-Gel books royalties from Galderma for Epsolay and Twyneo together (the quote; quarterly releases give e.g. '$0.5 million in royalty revenue from Galderma' for 2Q25), so even the royalty is not Epsolay-specific, and a royalty is not net sales. Galderma's releases give net sales by product category with only Nemluvio broken out (FY2025 appendix: Therapeutic Dermatology 780 / 1,185, 'of which Nemluvio 23 / 452'). Mayne Pharma's FY2025 annual report and FY2026 results name Epsolay only as an acquisition and launch, with no figure. No isolated Epsolay sales figure exists in any document checked.

source_quote: Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, Q4 2025 report (full-year 2025 figures), Healthcare net sales by major product lines/products (EUR million, 2025 | share | organic | currency | portfolio | total change | 2024 | share): Oncology 1,926 22% 0.3% -4.5% – -4.2% 2,009 24% | thereof: Erbitux 1,176 14% ... 1,162 14% | thereof: Bavencio 612 7% ... 735 9% (no Tepmetko line)
details: Merck KGaA (EMD Serono in the U.S.) is the only seller and has no partner or royalty holder on tepotinib. Its most detailed product table ('Net sales by major product lines/products', every quarterly and annual report 2019Q1-2026Q2) names only Erbitux and Bavencio under Oncology; from 2026Q1 the table was regrouped (Specialty Care: Erbitux, Bavencio, Mavenclad, Rebif) and still has no Tepmetko row. The unlisted Oncology remainder cannot be read as Tepmetko: in 2019Q1, a year before the first Tepmetko approval (Japan, announced 25 March 2020), Oncology 229 less Erbitux 199 less Bavencio 22 already left 8, so the remainder contains other products. The earnings presentations (2023Q4-2025Q3) stack Bavencio, Erbitux and Tepmetko in a 'Sales development Oncology' chart but print data labels only for the franchise totals and the Bavencio and Erbitux charts, never a Tepmetko value (pdfplumber text of the 2024Q4 deck p.40). Issuer documents give Tepmetko only organic growth rates (e.g. '+43% org.' FY2024, '+25% org.' Q4 2024, '+41% org.' Q2 2025). No isolated euro figure for Tepmetko exists in any document checked.

source_quote: Other pharmaceutical primarily reflects sales of other human health pharmaceutical products, including products within the franchises not listed separately. (Merck Form 10-K for 2025, product sales table, footnote 4 to the 'Other pharmaceutical' line; the table lists no Steglatro, Segluromet or Steglujan line)
details: Steglatro, Segluromet and Steglujan (ertugliflozin) are marketed by Merck in a Merck/Pfizer collaboration (revenues and certain costs shared 60%/40%; Pfizer records its 40% share as product sales of API supplied to Merck). Merck's most detailed product table (earnings release and 10-Q/10-K product sales disclosure, 2017Q4-2026Q2) has no ertugliflozin line; sales sit in 'Other pharmaceutical'. Across all Merck SEC filings 'Steglatro' occurs in only 20 documents (EDGAR full-text), all approval, collaboration, patent or litigation text (the 2025 10-K mentions it only in a DOJ civil investigative demand). Pfizer's filings mention ertugliflozin only for milestones ($90 million 2017, $60 million FDA approval, $40 million EU approval) and the 60/40 sharing terms; no Pfizer table or text prints ertugliflozin product revenue. No isolated sales figure (quarter, year or cumulative) exists in either issuer's documents.

source_quote: BENDEKA and TREANDA combined revenues in our United States segment in the second quarter of 2026 were $28 million
details: Teva, the only seller, prints one combined line for its two bendamustine brands in every revenue table from Bendeka's January 2016 launch to 2026Q2: 'Treanda and Bendeka' (6-K results releases 2016Q1-2017Q3, e.g. Q1 2016 155, Q2 2016 207, Q3 2016 149, Q4 2016 150), 'Bendeka and Treanda' / 'BENDEKA / TREANDA' (8-K and 10-Q/10-K segment tables 2017Q4-2026Q2) and the sentence quoted. Eagle Pharmaceuticals (licensor) prints only its own royalty income (e.g. 'BENDEKA royalties were $26.0 million in the first quarter of 2019, compared to $34.0 million in the first quarter of 2018') and changes in it, never Teva's net sales; converting royalties to sales would need an assumed effective rate (stepped from 20% to 25% to 30-32%), which is estimation. Only isolated figure: Eagle's 10-Qs/10-K for 2017 state that Teva 'reached $500 million in cumulative net sales of Bendeka' in 2017Q1 - a cumulative milestone, not a period's sales. No series exists, quarterly or annual.

source_quote: The Company does not disclose net sales for any products considered competitively sensitive.
details: Viatris prints net sales only for its select key global and segment products and states it does not disclose net sales for products it considers competitively sensitive; Perforomist is never a row. Prior owners: Mylan Inc. (Dey) from the October 2007 launch to 2015, and Mylan N.V. 2015-2020, describe it only qualitatively inside the Specialty segment (e.g. Q1 2009 release: Specialty 'third-party sales of $79.4 million ... Perforomist ... was the primary driver of the increase'; 10-K FY2008: 'Approximately 31% ... of the Company's Specialty Segment net revenues were attributable to bronchodilators, primarily DuoNeb, Perforomist and albuterol'; 10-Q Q2 2013 and 10-K FY2014/FY2015: Perforomist sales 'increased by double digits'). Isolated figures: none for the brand. The only amounts near the name are Specialty segment totals (EpiPen, Perforomist, DuoNeb and others) and a 2008 EPS impact estimate ('$0.20 to $0.25 negative impact' of the slower launch, 8-K 2008-02-27). source_quote: The Company generated approximately $144 million in new product revenues (as defined in “Certain Key Terms” below) in the third quarter (approximately $350 million for the year) primarily driven by lenalidomide, unbranded insulin glargine and interchangeable Semglee® in the U.S.
details: Semglee is named in Viatris and Mylan documents only in prose and, in the Viatris earnings releases of 2022, inside an aggregate 'new product revenues' figure shared with lenalidomide and unbranded insulin glargine. It is absent from the 'Select Key Global Products' and 'Select Key Segment Products' tables of every Viatris earnings release and 10-K 2021-2026, and the 10-Ks state that the company does not disclose net sales for products considered competitively sensitive. The partner Biocon (Biocon Biologics) reports only segment totals (Generics, Biosimilars, Research services) and Semglee market share, and its own deck combines Semglee with the unbranded glargine in one market-share line ('Includes both Semglee and unbranded Glargine'); Biocon Biologics Inc (US) accounts show one 'Traded Goods' revenue line. The brand was sold to Biocon Biologics in November 2022, so Viatris reporting of the brand ended then, and no successor document read prints a Semglee-only sales figure. Biocon Biologics' FY25 annual report and the Biocon Integrated Annual Report FY25 give only market share ('Market shares of our Semglee and Insulin Glargine franchise continue to be in mid-to-high-teens'), and the Q4 FY25 release says 'four biosimilars recording sales of USD 200 million each in FY25' without naming them. Isolated figures: none for Semglee; Viatris prints it only inside 'new product revenues' (with lenalidomide and unbranded insulin glargine) and inside 'Revenues from the biosimilars portfolio to be contributed to Biocon Biologics totaled approximately $167 million' (Q2 2022 release).

source_quote: The Company does not disclose net sales for any products considered competitively sensitive.
details: Viatris names Wixela Inhub among the 'significant products sold by the Developed Markets segment' in its 10-Ks and 10-Q prose (lower U.S. net sales due to competition) but never prints a figure; it is absent from the 'Select Key Global Products' and 'Select Key Segment Products' tables in every earnings release and 10-K 2021-2026. Mylan N.V. (FDA approval 2019-01-30) described it as a driver of North America new-product sales (10-Q Q3 2019, 10-K FY2019) without a figure. The ANDA is Mylan's; no partner reports its sales. source_quote: The ProAir line of products includes ProAir hydrofluoroalkane (“HFA”), ProAir RespiClick ® and ProAir Digihaler™, which are sold only in the United States.
details: Teva prints one ProAir line covering ProAir HFA (from 2010Q4), ProAir RespiClick (launched May 2015) and ProAir Digihaler (from July 2020), and never a RespiClick figure on its own; the line stops after 2021Q4.
